entries.title: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
entries.snippet: The promoter and broadcaster helped define the music tastes of Australians for decades.

entries.snippet: The official 2026 White House Christmas tree is an 18-foot fir from Silent Night Evergreens, a farm in Endeavor, Wisconsin.

entries.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
entries.snippet: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?

entries.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
entries.snippet: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

entries.snippet: Trump's meme coin dinners have sparked intense controversy. These two guests attended his latest on Sunday — and agreed to provide NPR inside access.

entries.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
entries.snippet: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.

entries.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
entries.snippet: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.

entries.snippet: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

entries.title: Meet Colombia's fuzzy 'water guardians'
entries.snippet: High in the Colombian Andes, a growing number of volunteers are racing to save an unusual plant that helps supply water to millions — one tiny seedling at a time.

entries.snippet: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.

entries.title: The science of how pets see and respond to screens
entries.snippet: Have you ever been sitting on your couch, watching a TV show, and noticed your dog is paying attention to the screen? A recent social media trend has raised new questions about how our canine friends engage with shows and movies. William Brangham reports.

entries.title: What's driving up the cost of Thanksgiving dinner
entries.snippet: As we approach Thanksgiving, Americans are heading to the grocery store ahead of the traditional meal with family and friends. But how much will that turkey and the fixings cost you this year? Digital reporter Tim McPhillips breaks down the numbers.

entries.title: What military families see as their biggest challenges as Trump's new military spouse commission convenes
entries.snippet: Military spouses interviewed by PBS News say there is more to do to improve quality of life for military families.

entries.snippet: The House Ethics Committee said in a report released Monday that there is "substantial evidence" that Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez of California engaged in sexual misconduct by making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer.

entries.snippet: The decision moves the case to a federal court, where Trump could seek to have charges dismissed on immunity grounds.

entries.title: Airline glitches and storms could make Thanksgiving travel messy
entries.snippet: A cascade of technical glitches that have upended airlines over the past week are adding to the unease.

entries.snippet: President Donald Trump says he will defer to a federal appeals court on whether to proceed with detonating degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant.

entries.snippet: The Democratic Party's incoming senators face an early test of their campaign promises to shake up Washington as they decide who will lead their new majority.

entries.snippet: The White House said the speech would be about protecting American families and Newsom's decision to commute the death sentences of more than 500 inmates to punishments of life without parole.

entries.title: Writers unhappy with PEN America's response to war in Gaza form new chapter
entries.snippet: Novelist Maaza Mengiste says they don't seek rivalry with PEN America but differ in structure and priorities.

entries.title: Some sheriffs who signed pacts to help Trump's immigration enforcement efforts ousted by voters
entries.snippet: Trump has encouraged local law enforcement agencies to sign partnerships with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. More than 2,700 agreements are in place nationwide.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies keep investing in Ukraine
entries.snippet: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.

entries.title: How the AI trade could trap even cautious investors
entries.snippet: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

entries.title: EU imposes import quotas for hybrid vehicles from China
entries.snippet: The EU is trying to protect its own car manufacturers from what it called "overcapacity" in China. Carmakers in the bloc, especially in Germany, have been lagging behind their Chinese rivals.

entries.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
entries.snippet: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.

entries.title: Istanbul 'lion hunt' ends with no big cat found after all
entries.snippet: After a major search operation for a lion on the loose in Istanbul woodlands, Turkish authorities said "the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat."

entries.title: Pakistani astronaut to join Chinese space mission
entries.snippet: A Pakistani astronaut is set to become to the first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a payload specialist, will join the Shenzhou-24 mission when it launches on Wednesday.

entries.title: Chinese official gets death sentence in spy case, report says
entries.snippet: A Chinese official recruited while working abroad was paid more than a million yuan to leak secrets, state-affiliated media reported.

entries.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
entries.snippet: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

entries.title: Germany news: Volkswagen begins wage talks with IG Metall union
entries.snippet: Germany's largest labor union IG Metall and automaker Volkswagen are holding wage negotiations, as the company looks to embark on cost-cutting measures. Meanwhile, Germany's president is in Ghana. DW has more.

entries.title: Exiled leader Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh on Dec. 16
entries.snippet: After two years of exile in India, ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has set a return date to Bangladesh. She was sentenced to death in absentia last year over a brutal crackdown that left hundreds dead.

entries.title: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy
entries.snippet: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.

entries.title: India: Report warns of deepening authoritarianism under Modi
entries.snippet: A Human Rights Watch report found that Modi's rule in India has eroded the rule of law and "systematically weakened institutions" meant to protect freedoms. Also, in Delhi a man injured nine police with a knife.

entries.title: US adds Megaspeed, at center of Nvidia scandal, to a trade blacklist
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist after tensions over its failure to do so raised questions. The news came the same day that Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO.

entries.title: Denmark: Top court backs hardline immigration "ghetto law"
entries.snippet: Denmark's Supreme Court has found that evictions of "non-Western" residents do not amount to discrimination. The government in Copenhagen argues its "ghetto law" encourages integration.

entries.title: Tajikistan follows US call, withdraws from ICC
entries.snippet: Tajikistan has initiated its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court as the US calls for it to be "dismantled." The decision was made during a recent visit from Russian President Vladimir Putin.

entries.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
entries.snippet: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.

entries.title: After Japan's APEC snub, what's next for its China ties?
entries.snippet: Japan has long-running concerns over Chinese military expansionism, and Beijing has bristled at Sanae Takaichi's comments on Taiwan. The frosty ties were on full display at the APEC summit.

entries.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
entries.snippet: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

entries.title: Nepal's new PM eyes closer ties with India amid lingering disputes
entries.snippet: On his first foreign bilateral visit, rapper-turned-Prime Minister Balendra Shah sought deeper ties with Nepal's neighbor and largest trading partner, while steering clear of sticky territorial issues.
